absent: Storage definitions and default values for image size, reserved size, resume file, resume block, resume wait, resume delay, no resume, no hibernate, no compress and hibernate compressor buffers.
Creation and lifetime of power object, suspend statistics lock initialization, wakelocks tree and lock initialization, filesystem sync workqueue and wait queue.
Behavior of suspend, hibernate, autosleep state setter, wakeup count save and query, active wakeup source printing, wake lock and unlock helpers, and memory device activity check.
Full suspend state enumeration values, platform suspend labels, memory sleep states table, and current memory sleep default.
Failure step enumeration values, step failure counter update sites, success and failure counter update sites, and error history recording beyond device names.
Macro expansion details for read only attributes and per step attributes, and sysfs operation table wiring for each attribute.
Power notifier chain head definition and notification payload contract.
Saved address space mask and count usage, and filesystem sync scheduling policy.

findings.text: Power core exposes registration helpers for power event notification. One adds a caller supplied block to a shared chain head and the other removes it, each returning the chain operation result.

Sleep transition query reports whether either a suspend transition or a hibernation transition is in progress. A companion predicate gates debug output on both a global debug flag and an in progress transition.
Suspend statistics reporters accumulate hardware sleep durations and record a maximum value. A separate helper records a failed device name into a small rotating history under a dedicated mutex.

Filesystem sync helper performs a full sync while measuring elapsed time and emitting an informational message. A workqueue function invokes that helper then decrements a shared counter and wakes waiters when it reaches zero.
Wakelock listing walks an ordered tree under a dedicated mutex and renders names whose active state matches the requested filter, with entries separated and terminated for sysfs display.

Image size and reserved size controls each present an unsigned long value as text on read. On write they accept a leading unsigned decimal number and update the stored value, returning the full input length on success and an invalid argument failure otherwise.

Boolean style power controls for async operation, sync on suspend, print times and debug messages show zero or one. Stores parse base ten unsigned input, reject parse failure and values above one, and otherwise update the corresponding flag.

Memory sleep selection display enumerates configured sleep labels in state order, bracketing the current selection, suppressing deep entries while a memory device mode is active, and ending output with a newline. Store path refuses change while autosleep holds an active state, decodes the label up to newline, and only accepts a genuine sleep state.

System state control lists available suspend labels plus a hibernation keyword when hibernation is available. Decoding checks the hibernation keyword first, then suspend labels by exact length match, otherwise yielding the on state. Store maps the generic memory request through the current memory sleep selection before dispatching to suspend or hibernate, and refuses work while autosleep is active.

Autosleep display reports off for the on state, otherwise the matching suspend label or disk or error depending on build options. Its store accepts the same vocabulary as system state plus an explicit off word, applies the memory sleep indirection, and delegates to the autosleep state setter.

Power test selection display enumerates test labels from first to max with the active level bracketed. Store trims at newline, holds the system sleep lock while scanning for an exact label match, updates the global level on match, and reports invalid argument otherwise.

Wakeup count read returns the current counter or an interrupted failure. Store refuses change while autosleep is active, parses an unsigned value, attempts to save it as the reference, and on mismatch prints active sources while returning invalid argument.

Wake lock and wake unlock style controls delegate display to active or inactive listing helpers and delegate mutation to dedicated lock or unlock helpers, returning full input length on success and propagating helper errors.

Resume boot options copy a resume path and optionally parse a numeric resume block offset, each ignored when no resume mode is set. Related flags enable resume wait, parse a resume delay with a warning on bad input, and jointly disable resume and hibernation for no hibernate forms.

Hibernate option parser distinguishes no resume, no compress, combined disable, and conditional image protection forms by prefix match, setting the corresponding global flags and invoking image protection enablement only when the strict executable protection build option is present.

Compressor selection only accepts names present in a build dependent allowlist. A successful match updates both the parameter store and a separate algorithm name buffer. Failures produce a debug message and propagate the error.
Restore image protection defaults to a no operation inline form in one build variant and to setting a persistent boolean flag in the snapshot variant.

Suspend statistics presentation keeps two entry rotating histories for failed device names, error numbers and failed steps. Sysfs last value views resolve the most recent slot by backward index arithmetic, while a sequential display dumps success and failure totals, per step counters and ordered histories.

Hardware sleep counters are visible in sysfs only when low power idle support is indicated, while all other suspend statistics entries use a fixed read only mode. A debug filesystem file exposes the same statistics through a sequential display operation.

Wakeup interrupt display reports no data when no interrupt is recorded and otherwise shows the recorded interrupt number. Print times initialization copies a global initcall debug flag in one variant and does nothing in the other.
Compressor parameter update uses a non blocking attempt on the system transition mutex and immediately reports busy when the mutex is held. Successful acquisition is always released before returning.

Failed device recording serializes history slot selection and name copy under a dedicated suspend statistics mutex. Wakelock listing holds a dedicated wakelocks mutex across the whole ordered tree walk.

Power test update holds the system sleep lock across label matching and global level assignment. Memory sleep, system state and wakeup count stores each acquire an autosleep lock, reject the operation with busy when autosleep is active, and release the lock on every exit path.

Suspend statistics record holds per step failure counters sized by number of steps, success and failure totals, rotating histories of depth two for device names plus error numbers plus step identifiers with separate indices, last plus total plus maximum hardware sleep durations, and an enumeration of step names.

Disk power group aggregates disk, resume offset, resume, image size and reserved size attributes under one group attached to the power object. Suspend statistics group aggregates success, failure, per step failures, last failure details and hardware sleep counters under a named subgroup with a custom visibility callback.

Suspend progress moves through working, freeze, prepare, suspend, late suspend, no interrupt suspend, then mirrored resume phases back to resume. Each phase has a fixed short label used for failure accounting and display, with working mapped to an empty label.

Power test levels form an ordered progression from none through core, processors, platform, devices and freezer. Resume and hibernation boot flags form a small latch where disable options force no resume and optionally no hibernate, and later resume path parsing observes that latch.

Early initialization creates the disk attribute group under the power object and creates a debug filesystem statistics file. Global async default is enabled unless an explicit off boot option is supplied, and debug message output defaults off unless its boot option is present.

Boot command handlers provide resume path, resume offset, hibernate control, no resume, resume wait, resume delay, no hibernate, async control and debug message entry points, each returning success after consuming its argument.

Several sysfs stores update shared globals without visible serialization, including image size, reserved size, async enable, sync on suspend, print times, debug flag and current memory sleep selection, so concurrent writers can interleave. Hardware sleep accumulators are also updated without holding the statistics mutex used for failure history.

Numeric sysfs parsing accepts a valid prefix and ignores trailing characters in some controls, while label decoding uses exact length matching up to newline. Failure history retains only two records, so older failures are silently overwritten, and visibility of hardware sleep counters depends on platform firmware flags.

Filesystem sync wakeup resolution is five. Failure history depth is two. Number of suspend steps aliases the resume step identifier. Suspend statistics file uses regular file read permissions for all users.

Test labels are none, core, processors, platform, devices and freezer in level order. Suspend step labels are empty for working, then freeze, prepare, suspend, suspend late, suspend no interrupt, resume no interrupt, resume early and resume.
